text: hey clone this repo, and tell me how it works, and if we can get an attempt to recreate the same approach for our 3d modeling @cart/hmsc-int/editors/model/Studio.tsx or what https://github.com/lightningpixel/modly
resolution: Cloned lightningpixel/modly and analyzed its architecture: Electron+React frontend (Three.js viewport, @xyflow node-graph) over a Python FastAPI backend that runs open-source GPU diffusion models (Hunyuan3D-2 Mini, TripoSG, Trellis2) as installable GitHub extensions; image->dense-triangle-GLB, with mesh-remesher/optimizer/uv_unwrapper/texture_baker post-process nodes. Assessed reuse for cart/hmsc-int/editors/model/Studio.tsx: do NOT embed the generator (Electron + GPU Python server is incompatible with our V8-only no-node cart runtime) — keep generation offline like the existing importPropMesh.mjs CLI. The high-value bridge is import-into-editable-Studio: the GLB/OBJ parser already exists (importPropMesh.mjs, 624 lines, used for Desk.glb) but only bakes static render-only ImportedProp triangle soup; Studio's editable model is EditMesh (verts + n-gon faces) and addPart() already accepts any EditMesh (addCube is just addPart(cuboid())). The single missing piece is a trianglesToEditMesh() converter (~100 lines, inverse of existing editMeshToGeometry), plus a Studio Import action. Key caveat surfaced: raw AI meshes are dense blobs needing decimation/retopo (modly's own remesher) before they are hand-editable low-poly. Recommended minimal slice = the import bridge verified on Desk.glb (316 verts), generator deferred. No code changed; this is an assessment/answer.
